In its sustainability report, the company states that it does not track enteric and manure emissions from live animal operations and only reports on enteric fermentation from animals on its own feedlots and farms.

Although the company states its net-zero target covers the entire supply chain, the lack of disclosure of its entire emissions footprint makes it questionable whether enteric fermentation of non-JBS farms and deforestation emissions – accounting for an estimated 97% of JBS’s emission footprint – are covered under the net-zero.
JBS states it wants to eliminate (illegal) deforestation but does not clarify whether this is part of its offsetting strategy or a measure for reducing supply chain emissions.
JBS’s entire emissions footprint is estimated at 280 MtCO2e; yet the company reports less than 3% of this.
